summary: Intercontinental multipath crossover causing chunked response delays for streaming inference
description:
Issue summary: Customer Lumenly reports elevated streaming latency and chunked responses when sending long-form chat prompts.
Impact: Multiple production customers using the dedicated pool (account LUM-42) see increased P50->P99 tail on streamed tokens; some sessions experience repeated TCP-level stalls and client perceived stalls for 2-10s.
Timeline: 2026-03-13 08:12 UTC - first alert from Lumenly (support chat); 2026-03-13 08:25 UTC - automated p99 latency alert for us-west serving group; 2026-03-13 08:40 UTC - support ticket created; 2026-03-13 09:10 UTC - SRE and Serving triaged.
Environment: Dedicated capacity (pool dcap-lum-01) in us-west-2 region that routes synthetic traffic to eu-west-1 compute for certain models.
Steps to reproduce: 1) Send a streaming chat request via API key for account LUM-42 with a 2k token prompt. 2) Observe initial tokens stream, then a 1-8s stall before the next chunk. 3) Repeated attempts sometimes succeed without stall (non-deterministic).
Observed behavior: Streaming connection remains open, but token emission is chunked with long inter-chunk gaps rather than steady token rate. No 5xx returned to client.
Relevant logs & metrics:
- Gateway traces show request flapped between route candidates (primary path us-west-2 -> eu-west-1 direct and alternate us-west-2 -> transit -> eu-west-1) with different RTTs.
- TCP-level retransmit spike on the alternate path during stall windows (see packet_loss:0.8%-1.5% in tcpdump snippets).
- Serving runtime token generation CPU/GPU traces show no lock contention; KV cache hit ratio unchanged.
- Per-account routing policy indicates multipath routing enabled for cost-savings.
Hypothesis: A short-lived multipath crossover at the egress layer is switching packets between different underlay paths (one with transient packet loss / higher latency), producing backpressure at the streaming layer and chunked token emission.
Immediate mitigations attempted: 1) Disabled multipath routing for LUM-42 (traffic pinned to primary path) at 2026-03-13 09:35 UTC — preliminary reduction in stalls observed for repro tests. 2) Applied temporary routing weight bias away from transit path at 09:50 UTC.
Next steps: 1) SRE to confirm transit provider packet loss during windows (netops ticket INT-4021). 2) Serving/runtime to add additional fine-grained retry/backoff on inter-chunk writes for streaming SDK paths. 3) Monitor p50/p95/p99 for next 24h and validate with customer.
Notes: Customer impact: high for Lumenly (video captioning pipeline), causing visible downstream backlog in their ingestion queues.

investigation_notes: Packet captures show 0.8%-1.5% retransmit on alternate transit path during stalls.
Route selection score oscillates when BGP path preference changes on provider A's edge for a 20-45s window.
Serving runtime token generator latency stable; stalls align with network-level retransmits and increased RTT variance.
Disabling multipath for the account reduced observed stalls in 8/10 synthetic test runs.
Related internal ticket INT-4021 opened to collect provider-side telemetry and BGP updates.

Potential longer-term fixes: improve route stickiness for streaming sessions; detect transient packet loss and auto-failover to stable path rather than oscillating; or disable multipath for latency-sensitive streaming routes by default.
resolution:
Mitigation: Multipath routing disabled for LUM-42 (temporary) and routing weight bias applied to avoid transit path. Auto-pin alert created to detect oscillation and pin traffic automatically.
Permanent action items: Netops to coordinate with transit provider to address transient packet loss (INT-4021). Product to evaluate changing default multipath policy for streaming workloads and add SDK-side backoff for chunk writes.
Status: Mitigation in place; monitoring for recurrence. Customer scheduled for post-incident review.
